region.text: Etelköz, 'the lands between the Lower Danube and the Don River in the 870s'

ledger.note: c. 840: the Magyars settle the Etelköz, between the Carpathians and the Dnieper. The Hungarians page: 'Around 830, a rebellion broke out in the Khazar khaganate' and the Hungarians moved to 'the Etelköz, the territory between the Carpathians and the Dnieper River'; the Etelköz page puts the exodus from Levedia 'around 850'. Confidence 1: Cliopatria's 840 bridges two pages that differ by twenty years. The Hungarians were 'subordinates of the Khazar Khaganate' around the Don (page). Second page, Levedia: 'the Magyars lived in Levedia in the vicinity of the Khazar Khaganate in the early 9th century' with the start 'either before 750 (István Fodor) or around 830 (Gyula Kristó)', 'the Magyars' forced exodus from Levedia occurred around 850', and they 'controlled the lands between the Lower Danube and the Don River in the 870s'; the Khazars page: the Pechenegs' 'first attack ... around 854', raids from the Etelköz into the Basin 'from 862 onwards'. Still confidence 1: no page dates the arrival in Etelköz, so 840 is a bridge.

region.text: the western and northern edge of the Magyars' 882-883 shape that the 884 shape drops: 58 cells, 14,668 km2, 26.1-30.2E, 45.4-51.0N

ledger.note: 884: Cliopatria's Magyars shape shrinks by 14,668 km2 while its Kievan Rus' shape grows into the same cells (57 of the 58 cells are in Kievan Rus' 884; none in 882). Oleg page: Oleg seized Kiev in '881-882' and 'In 883, Oleg made the Drevlians pay tribute to Kiev'; it is silent on the Severians (884), the Radimichs and on any Magyar land. The Khazars page: 'By the 880s, Khazar control of the Middle Dnieper from Kiev ... began to wane'. Confidence 1: no page says the Magyars held this land or lost it; the loss is bridged from the two Cliopatria shapes. The kievan-rus dossier (eu-16, not yet written) owes the mirror gain.

region.text: the steppe east of the Dnieper: 'drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892'

ledger.note: By 892: the Pechenegs drive the Magyars west of the Dnieper. 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889', the Pechenegs 'in turn drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892'. The region is the part of the 887 shape that Cliopatria drops by 896; the north of it is not explained by the page.

c. 895: a Pecheneg invasion drives the Magyars out of Etelköz. 'A new Pecheneg invasion compelled the Magyars to leave Etelköz and cross the Carpathian Mountains around 895.' The Hungarian conquest page: 'a joint attack by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians in 894 or 895'; the Pechenegs page: they 'drove out the Magyars remaining in Etelköz'. Cliopatria holds the Etelköz to 899.

'In 895/896, under the leadership of Árpád, some Hungarians crossed the Carpathians and entered the Carpathian Basin.' The region is Cliopatria's 896 addition (about 121,000 km2) without the 210 cells that Great Moravia's 892-895 shape holds (see the 896 gain from great-moravia); the Principality of Hungary's own dossier carries the Pannonian side.

region.text: the lower Dniester steppe taken from Bulgaria in the war of 894-896

ledger.note: Cliopatria 896-897: the Magyars hold the lower Dniester steppe. The Hungarians 'invaded Bulgaria, forced Tzar Simeon to flee to the fortress of Dristra'. Confidence 1: the page gives neither a year nor the land; the war began in 894 (Leo VI's break with the Bulgarians), Cliopatria's shape moves in 896. Second page, Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 894-896: 'in 895, the Byzantine navy sailed to the Danube Delta to assist the Magyars' and the Magyars 'ravaged Dobruja and dealt a heavy defeat on the Bulgarian army' of Simeon I; the page says nothing about Bessarabia, the lower Dniester or any land taken, and the 896 treaty cedes only an 'area between the Black Sea and Strandzha' to Bulgaria.

region.text: the eastern Slovak lands and the upper Tisza held by Great Moravia's 892-895 shape: 210 cells, 53,109 km2, 19.1-23.4E, 47.5-49.5N

ledger.note: 896: the Hungarians enter land that Cliopatria's Great Moravia shape holds to 895. 'In 895/896, under the leadership of Árpád, some Hungarians crossed the Carpathians and entered the Carpathian Basin.' The great-moravia dossier loses the same 210 cells to magyars in 896 (before the review it lost them to nobody while this dossier gained them from nobody). Confidence 1: no page says the Magyars took this land from Moravia (a word search of the Hungarian conquest page for Tisza, Slovakia, Verecke and Subcarpathia finds no statement that the land belonged to Great Moravia or was taken from it; it has only 'the territories east of the river Tisza'); the overlap is Cliopatria geometry and the Great Moravia page's eastern lands since Rastislav.

region.text: the lower Dniester steppe, returned to Bulgaria

ledger.note: 898: Bulgaria regains the steppe. 'The Bulgarians ... attacked and routed the Hungarians' (Porphyrogenitus, no year on the page); the year is Cliopatria's (Bulgaria's shape grows again in 898). Second page, Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 894-896: 'in the beginning of 896 the Bulgarians and Pechenegs attacked the Magyar homeland on two fronts', with a 'crushing defeat on the Magyars in the steppes along the Southern Bug'; the page does not mention 897 or 898 and names no land returned. region.text: the Basin lands that become the Principality of Hungary's own shape in 900

ledger.note: 900: the Hungarian core is drawn as the Principality of Hungary. Principality page: 'established around 895'; the Hungarians were 'firmly establishing their state there by 900'. Confidence 1: the split between the 'Magyars' and 'Principality of Hungary' rows is Cliopatria's; the page does not date a division of land. Kurszán page: 'at the turn of the 9th and 10th centuries' he was 'kende of the Magyars in the dual leadership with Árpád serving as a gyula'; no division of land is dated.

region.text: the tribal territories of the east, among them Transylvania

ledger.note: c. 907: the tribal confederation becomes the single Principality under Árpád and his heirs. The Principality page: 'After Kurszán's death this division ceased and Árpád became the sole ruler'; the kende rule ends 'c. 904' (infobox) or 907 (text); Kurszán's death is dated 902 or 904 (Hungarian conquest page). Gyula's Transylvania stayed semi-independent (page). Kurszán page: Kurszán 'died 904', murdered with his entourage at the river Fischa when Louis the Child invited them in the summer of 904, and 'From this point Árpád became the only ruler'; the page dates the attack on Great Moravia with Arnulf to 892/893 and says nothing of 902, of the Principality or of 907. The sole rule therefore dates from 904 on this page; the end year 907 follows the Principality page and stays confidence 1.

region.text: the Magyar tribal lands east of the Principality's core

ledger.note: 907: the Magyar row ends; the land continues under the Principality of Hungary. Árpád's rule is 'c. 895 to c. 907' (infobox); the Battle of Pressburg was fought 4-6 July 907. Cliopatria keeps the row to 910. Kurszán page: Kurszán 'died 904', murdered with his entourage at the river Fischa when Louis the Child invited them in the summer of 904, and 'From this point Árpád became the only ruler'; the page dates the attack on Great Moravia with Arnulf to 892/893 and says nothing of 902, of the Principality or of 907. The sole rule therefore dates from 904 on this page; the end year 907 follows the Principality page and stays confidence 1.

wars.name: Pecheneg drive-out of the Magyars from Etelköz
wars.outcome: The Pechenegs, 'Driven further west by the Khazars and Cumans by 889', 'drove the Magyars west of the Dnieper River by 892' and then 'drove out the Magyars remaining in Etelköz'; Simeon I of Bulgaria 'employed the Pechenegs to help fend off the Magyars' (undated).
wars.note: The Etelköz page puts the departure 'around 895'; the Hungarian conquest page 'a joint attack by the Pechenegs and Bulgarians in 894 or 895'.

wars.name: Hungarian-Bulgarian war of 894-896
wars.outcome: The Byzantines invaded Bulgaria from the south as the Hungarians attacked from the north; Simeon fled to Dristra; 'The Bulgarians ... attacked and routed the Hungarians'. Cliopatria shows the steppe Magyar in 896-897. Byzantine-Bulgarian war page: in 895 the Magyars 'ravaged Dobruja and dealt a heavy defeat on the Bulgarian army'; 'in the beginning of 896 the Bulgarians and Pechenegs attacked the Magyar homeland on two fronts' and defeated the Magyars on the Southern Bug; the page names no land taken or returned.
wars.note: The page gives 894 for the start ('Contemporaneous sources suggest that the invasion followed the 894 Bulgarian-Byzantine war') and no end year.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of the Carpathian Basin

zones.text: Transylvania and the east, the Magyar lands beside the Principality

wars.outcome: The Hungarians crossed the Carpathians in 895/896, took Pannonia in 900, defeated Great Moravia in 902 and beat the Bavarians at Pressburg on 4 July 907; the tribal territories east of the core stayed semi-independent.
wars.note: The Principality of Hungary's own dossier carries the Pannonian side; this entry records the eastern lands.

certainty.note: A nomadic confederation's range: the Etelköz is described by rivers (Dnieper, Dniester, Prut, Siret) and the Muslim sources by two others; no frontier is fixed on any page.

notes: Magyars (Cliopatria 'Magyars' 840-910), eu-15-a. This is the pre-conquest confederation in Etelköz and then the eastern tribal lands; the Hungarian state of the Basin is the Principality of Hungary (another dossier, Cliopatria 900-999). The Etelköz was lost to the Pechenegs (a people Cliopatria has no row for; counterpart 'pechenegs' needs a dossier, Pecheneg Khanates 889-1091) by 892 and in 895; Cliopatria holds it to 899, so the 896 and 898 shapes are corrected to the Carpathian side and the 887 shape is cut in 892. Start 840 bridges the Hungarians page (c. 830) and the Etelköz page (c. 850). The Khazar suzerainty ('subordinates of the Khazar Khaganate' around the Don; the Kabar revolt) is undated on the pages, so it is not in the ledger; the Khazaria dossier should carry any vassal event. Transylvania: Cliopatria's Principality of Hungary shape (16.3-23.5E) stops west of it; this dossier hands the eastern lands to the Principality at 907 and the Hungary dossiers should extend the Principality to cover Transylvania 907-1000 (Gyula's domain 'semi-independent'). The 892 and 895 losses use shape arithmetic on Cliopatria's own shapes (intersect/minus of the 887 and 896 years); the 896 shape also holds a lower Dniester steppe Bulgaria loses to the Magyars (Bulgaria's shape shrinks 896-897 and regains it 898). No capital: the pages name none (the kende and gyula led the confederation). Rulers are not listed (Levedi, Álmos and Árpád are not dated on the pages opened; Árpád 'c. 895 to c. 907' is in the Principality of Hungary dossier). Repair pass 2026-10-25 after the review: (1) the 895 gain of 121,392 km2 from nobody is split: 210 cells (53,109 km2) held by Great Moravia's 892-895 shape are now a 896 gain from great-moravia (mirror of great-moravia's 896 loss to magyars), the other 270 cells (68,283 km2) stay a 895 gain from nobody. (2) The 884 keyframe's -14,668 km2 now has a loss event to kievan-rus (confidence 1; Cliopatria geometry: 57 of 58 cells in Rus' 884; the Khazars page and the Oleg page do not mention Magyar land); kievan-rus (eu-16) owes the mirror gain. (3) Pages opened for the thin items: Khazars (silent on the 884 change), Levedia (start 840 still a bridge), Byzantine-Bulgarian war of 894-896 (no land named; Bessarabia and the lower Dniester not mentioned; the Hungarian conquest page, re-read with a word query, does carry 'The Hungarians invaded Bulgaria, forced Tzar Simeon to flee to the fortress of Dristra' and 'attacked and routed the Hungarians' (both undated; a broader summary query had missed them)), Kurszán (sole rule of Árpád from 904, which disagrees with the end year 907). The pechenegs dossier now exists and is dropped from the counterparts needing dossiers.
